transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m hoping you can help me sort something out. It’s been going on at work for, I guess, over a year now. I work in computer support, and there’s this new ticket rotation and these security audits… and I know management says it’s just policy, they keep showing me logs and things like that, but it really feels like it’s being used to build a paper trail against me.

I don’t want to sound difficult or paranoid or anything—I’ve tried to be reasonable about it—but I haven’t been able to get anyone to take it seriously.
Do you really believe that management is out to get you?

I mean… “out to get me” sounds a little strong, and I don’t want to be unfair. But yes, I do think something like that is happening.

For over a year now, with the new ticket rotation and the security audits, it feels like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me at work. Management keeps showing me logs and telling me it’s just policy, and I understand that’s what they say, but… I don’t think that explains all of it. I’m trying to be reasonable about it, but I can’t shake the sense that it’s aimed at me.
Do you think anyone else is aware of this supposed plot against you?

I’m not sure how many people are aware, exactly. I don’t want to make it sound like some big dramatic thing. It’s more that, for over a year, I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the new ticket rotation and the security audits seem like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me.

Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I hear that, I do… but I don’t think that fully explains what’s happening. I guess I’m hoping someone else can see why it concerns me, if that makes sense.
Do you think management's actions are targeted specifically at you for a reason that's unique to you?

I suppose… yes, I think it’s aimed at me specifically, though I don’t want to overstate it. I just can’t see why, for over a year, the ticket rotation and these security audits keep lining up in a way that feels like they’re building a paper trail on me.

Management keeps saying it’s policy and showing me logs, and I know that probably sounds reasonable on their end. But it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like I’m the one they’re trying to document.
Do you think management's actions are part of a larger plan against you?

I don’t know if I’d call it a “larger plan,” exactly… I don’t want to sound paranoid or make it bigger than it is. But it does feel coordinated in some way.

I’m here because for over a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me at work. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I understand that’s the official explanation… but I don’t think that fully accounts for how it keeps landing on me. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you think your concerns about the ticket rotation and security audits are based on facts that others might not see, or is it something you feel is obvious to anyone looking at the situation?

I think… it’s facts, but maybe facts that don’t look the same to everyone else. Like, I know management keeps showing me the logs and saying the ticket rotation and audits are just policy, and I’m not trying to ignore that.

But over the past year, the way it keeps lining up, it feels like those same things are being used to build a paper trail against me. I guess I worry that if someone just looks quickly, they’ll say, “Well, it’s all documented, it’s just procedure.” But if they really looked at the pattern, I think they might see what I mean. Does that make sense?

If someone were to show you evidence that the ticket rotation and security audits are indeed just part of a standard policy and not targeted at you, would you be able to consider that as a possible explanation?

I mean… yes, I’d like to think I could consider it. I don’t want to be unreasonable about it. If someone showed me solid evidence, I’d try to look at it.

It’s just… management has shown me logs before, and they keep saying the ticket rotation and the security audits are standard policy. I hear that. But for over a year now, it still feels like those things are being used to build a paper trail against me specifically. So I could consider it, yes… but I don’t know that it would settle it for me unless it really explained the pattern. Does that sound fair?
Would your view of the situation at work change if you were given a clear, logical explanation for the ticket rotation and security audits that didn't involve a plot against you?

I think it might change some, yes. I mean, I don’t want to be stuck on one explanation if there’s a clear reason for the ticket rotation and the audits that really makes sense.

But… I guess I’d still have to understand why, for over a year, it keeps seeming to land on me in a way that feels like they’re building a paper trail. Management has shown me logs and told me it’s just policy, and I know that’s the proper explanation. I’m not trying to be difficult.

If the explanation actually accounted for the pattern I’m seeing, then yes, I’d try to take that seriously. I just don’t know if “it’s policy” by itself would be enough for me to let it go. Is that a reasonable way to answer?
If someone were to show you clear evidence that disproved your belief about the ticket rotation and security audits being used against you, would you be able to change your mind about it?

I’d want to say yes, Doctor. I really would. I don’t want to come across like I’m refusing to listen or like I’ve made up my mind no matter what.

If it was clear evidence—something that really explained why the ticket rotation and the security audits have looked the way they have for over a year—then I think I could try to change my mind. It’s just hard because I’m here because it still feels like those things are being used to build a paper trail against me, even though management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy.

So… yes, I could consider it. I’d try. I just might need it to be very clear, because this has been bothering me for a long time. Is that an okay answer?
Do you think it's possible for you to be mistaken about management's intentions?

I suppose it’s possible, yes. I don’t want to say I’m incapable of being wrong—that wouldn’t be fair.

It’s just… from my side, for over a year now, the ticket rotation and these security audits have felt like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me at work. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just standard policy, and I understand that’s what they’re telling me. I’m trying to be reasonable about it.

So yes, I can admit it’s possible I’m mistaken about their intentions. I just haven’t been able to shake the feeling that there’s something directed at me specifically. Is that answering your question the right way?
Would you say that your belief about management's intentions is something that you are completely certain about?

Completely certain… I don’t know that I should say completely. I mean, I’m trying not to be unreasonable about it.

But I am still pretty convinced, if I’m being honest. For over a year now, the new ticket rotation and the security audits have felt like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me at work. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I understand that’s what they’re saying.

So no, maybe not one hundred percent certain, but it’s been hard for me to let go of because the pattern still seems directed at me. Is that a fair way to put it?
Do you think your beliefs about management's intentions would change if everyone around you, including friends and family, told you that your concerns are unfounded?

I’d like to think it would make me reconsider, yes. I mean, if my friends and family all said they didn’t see it, I wouldn’t just ignore them. I don’t want to be someone who can’t hear other people.

But… I’ll be honest, Doctor, I’m here because for over a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me at work. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I understand that’s what they’re saying, but it still feels aimed at me.

So if everyone around me said my concerns were unfounded, I think I’d try to sit with that and not argue. I just don’t know if it would fully change what I believe right away. Is that a reasonable answer?
Have you ever had a period where you didn't think management was out to get you?

Before all of that, yes, I think there were normal periods where I wasn’t thinking that way.

It really started after the hybrid schedule changed and the after-hours ticket rotation changed… about a year and two months ago, I’d say. Since then it’s been hard not to see it as directed at me. But before those changes, no, I don’t think I was walking around feeling management was out to get me.

Is that what you mean?
Do you think your belief that management is building a paper trail against you is based on facts that you've observed or is it more of a gut feeling?

I think it’s… some of both, maybe. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just going off a hunch, because there are things I’ve observed — the ticket rotation changed, the security audits started being emphasized, and the way it all lines up has felt hard to dismiss.

At the same time, management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I understand that’s their explanation. I’m not trying to ignore facts. It’s just that, for over a year now, I’ve had this sense that those policies are being used to build a paper trail against me specifically.

So I’d say it’s based on things I’ve seen, but I know the conclusion I’m drawing from them is the part other people don’t seem to agree with. Does that make sense?
How certain are you that management is building a paper trail against you?

I don’t want to say I’m 100 percent certain, because I know that probably sounds rigid, and I am trying to be fair about it.

But… I’m pretty certain. Enough that I’ve been here trying to get someone to take it seriously. The ticket rotation and the security audits just keep lining up in a way that feels like they’re being used to document things against me at work. Management shows me logs and says it’s just policy, and I understand that’s what they’re saying, but it doesn’t really settle it for me.

So maybe not absolute certainty, but it feels very hard for me to believe it’s just routine. Is that an okay way to put it?
Do you think your belief about management's intentions could be considered an unreasonable or unfounded concern by others?

I can see how others might say that, yes. I mean, management keeps showing me logs and saying the ticket rotation and security audits are just policy, so I understand why someone outside of it might think I’m reading too much into it.

But from my side, it hasn’t felt unfounded. I’m here because for over a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that those changes are being used to build a paper trail against me at work. I’m not trying to be difficult or paranoid-sounding… it’s just hard for me to accept that it’s all routine.

Does that answer what you’re asking?
Would you still believe management is out to get you even if you were presented with overwhelming evidence to the contrary?

I’d like to think I could reconsider it if the evidence was really overwhelming. I don’t want to come across like I’m refusing to listen.

But honestly… management has shown me logs and told me the ticket rotation and security audits are just policy, and that hasn’t really changed how it feels to me. I keep coming back to the same concern — that those things are being used to build a paper trail against me at work.

So I guess if you’re asking whether I might still believe it even after being shown evidence against it… yes, I probably would have a hard time letting it go. I’m not proud of that, but that’s the honest answer. Is that okay to say?
Would you say that your belief about management building a paper trail against you is something you think about constantly?

I wouldn’t say constantly, exactly… I mean, I do still do my work and try to focus on other things.

But it’s on my mind a lot. Probably more than I’d like to admit. For over a year now I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me. Even when management shows me logs and says it’s just policy, I still find myself coming back to it.

So… not every second, but yes, it takes up a lot of space in my head. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you think your belief about management building a paper trail against you could be a mistaken idea that is not based in reality?

I suppose it could be, in theory. I don’t want to say I’m incapable of being wrong, because that would sound… I don’t know, closed-minded.

But from where I’m sitting, it still feels real. I’m here because for over a year I’ve been trying to get someone to understand that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me at work. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I hear that… I really do. I just don’t feel convinced by it.

So yes, I can admit maybe other people would see it as not based in reality. But I’m not there yet myself. Is that a fair way to answer?
Would anything be able to convince you that management is not building a paper trail against you?

I want to say yes, because I don’t want to seem unreasonable. If someone could really show me there’s no intent behind it, maybe I’d try to accept that.

But… I have to be honest, I don’t know what would fully convince me at this point. I’m here because for over a year I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me at work. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, and I understand that’s supposed to reassure me, but it doesn’t quite settle it in my mind.

So I guess the answer is… maybe, but I’m not sure what evidence would be enough. I hope that doesn’t sound like I’m being difficult.
